text:
alex (infra): Heads-up — last 30m we've seen repeated GPU saturation in shared-pool-eu with oscillating latencies. top-10 tenants driving ~72% of queued tokens. thinking we need a smoothing shed + soft-credit system rather than hard preemption.
Maria Chen: Can you paste the metric spikes? is it bursty traffic or long-running seqs?
alex (infra): Mostly bursty. median seq length unchanged but arrival rate has spikes that blow up batching windows. screenshot: <link>
TJ: Are these from retry storms or legit user spikes? any tenant ids?
alex (infra): mix. two tenants (t-connex, t-chatty) have noisy short bursts. one tenant with long convo sessions causes KV cache pressure and slower eviction -> memory backpressure.
Søren: I'd prefer soft shaping so we don't gun for SLA misses. proposal outline: per-tenant leaky-bucket credits decaying over 10m, a global smoothing reservoir for short bursts, and an admission controller that throttles when reservoir < threshold. also prefer to degrade to smaller model variants before outright throttling.
jess (sre): +1. can we tie to useful signals: queue depth, live p99 latency, and available free GPUs? need simple tunables.
alex (infra): yep. rough policy YAML I mocked:
```yaml
admission:
  type: smoothing_shed
  per_tenant:
    bucket_capacity: 1000  # token units
    refill_rate: 5        # tokens/sec
    decay_window: 600     # seconds
  global_reservoir:
    capacity: 5000
    min_reserve: 800
    burst_window: 30
  fallbacks:
    - model_variant: small-quant
      condition: reservoir < 1200
    - action: rate_limit
      condition: reservoir < 400
      soft_percent: 20
```
Maria Chen: Nice. How do we measure "token units" for a mixed workload (embeddings + gen)?
Søren: map to normalized cost: gen-token=1, embed-request=0.5, rerank=0.2. we already have cost model in billing-service.
TJ: rollout plan?
alex (infra): Start in EU canary pool only (shared-pool-eu). Steps:
- deploy smoothing_shed in read-only mode (metrics only) for 1h
- enable soft-fallback to small-quant for 15% of traffic for noisy tenant candidates
- enable active shaping for top-5 noisy tenants; monitor p99/p50 and error rate for 2h
- revert if p99 increases > 10% or error rate > 0.5% above baseline
infra-bot: autoscaler detected sustained 95% GPU util in shared-pool-eu; scaling blocked by quota. Created ticket INF-4529.
jess (sre): quota blocking is problematic — if we scale we might mask the underlying fairness problem.
Maria Chen: Cost question: will smoothing push more requests to small-quant and inflate quality regressions? we need eval hooks.
alex (infra): Yes — integrate with Optimize's eval runner: run a small A/B on prompt set and monitor quality delta. if delta > threshold, back off to rate_limit not model swap.
TJ: How do we pick tenants to shape? static list or dynamic score?
Søren: dynamic scoring: noisy score = weighted(sum of burstiness, rate, cache-pressure). keep top-K > threshold. store scores in redis scoreboard with TTL.
Maria Chen: Any risk of tenant evading by spreading across api-keys/tenants?
alex (infra): We already have fingerprinting by org+sub-tenant headers and IP heuristics. edge cases exist but rare.
jess (sre): Obs: we need strong observability: per-tenant token burn, per-tenant queue depth, and a timeline of fallback events. add tagging on traces.
alex (infra): Yep — console patch incoming to show per-tenant "smoothing" events and rollback toggle.
TJ: Do we need legal/compliance sign-off for degrading models? might affect regulated customers.
Maria Chen: For enterprise-tier customers we should always prefer dedicated fallback or contact customer success before any model swap. add allowlist.
Søren: Implementation detail: prefer non-blocking admission: return HTTP 429 with Retry-After for rate limits; for model swap return 200 but annotate response header x-model-variant and x-smoothing-applied.
alex (infra): Good. Also let's add a short-circuit: if tenant is on Dedicated (dedicated tag) skip smoothing altogether.
infra-bot: deployment job queued: smoothing-shed v1 -> canary (shared-pool-eu). CI checks: unit, integration, policy-checks.
Maria Chen: timeline?
alex (infra): aim for canary tomorrow 08:00 UTC. I'll open a PR with the YAML + telemetry dashboards tonight. Please add any blocking concerns here.
TJ: lgtm from me. will watch p99 + infra-bot alerts.
Søren: lgtm but add a kill-switch feature flag for rapid rollback.
jess (sre): I'll coordinate on the incident channel and make runbook entries for INF-4529.
Maria Chen: Thanks — this looks pragmatic. :thumbsup:
alex (infra): Thanks all — I'll post PR + manifest shortly.
__note: This file is a synthetic Slack thread representing a single conversation about tenant fairness and smoothing/soft-shedding policies in the shared GPU pool. Messages are in chronological order and use short Slack-style replies.
